source_text:
Τῶν τοσούτων οὖν καὶ τοιούτων οὕτως μεμαρτυρημένων τὸ ταπεινόφρον καὶ τὸ ὑποδεὲς διὰ τῆς ὑπακοῆς οὐ μόνον ἡμᾶς, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰς πρὸ ἡμῶν γενεὰς βελτίους ἐποίησεν, τούς τε καταδεξαμένους τὰ λόγια αὐτοῦ ἐν φόβῳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ.
πολλῶν οὖν καὶ μεγάλων καὶ ἐνδόξων μετειληφότες πράξεων ἐπαναδράμωμεν ἐπὶ τὸν ἐξ ἀρχῆς παραδεδομένον ἡμῖν τῆς εἰρήνης σκοπόν, καὶ ἀτενίσωμεν εἰς τὸν πατέρα καὶ κτίστην τοῦ σύμπαντος κόσμου καὶ ταῖς μεγαλοπρεπέσι καὶ ὑπερβαλλούσαις αὐτοῦ δωρεαῖς τῆς εἰρήνης εὐεργεσίαις τε κολληθῶμεν.
ἴδωμεν αὐτὸν κατὰ διάνοιαν καὶ ἐμβλέψωμεν τοῖς ὄμμασιν τῆς ψυχῆς εἰς τὸ μακρόθυμον αὐτοῦ βούλημα: νοήσωμεν, πῶς ἀόργητος ὑπάρχει πρὸς πᾶσαν τὴν κτίσιν αὐτοῦ.
thought_title: The Humility of the Ancients and the Peace of God
orientation: Clement has just quoted Psalm 51 at length, and now he turns from the example of David's repentance to the general lesson that humility and obedience have made past generations better, and he calls the Corinthians to return to the goal of peace and to contemplate God's patient will.
pass_a_gloss: Of [the] so many therefore and such [things] thus having been witnessed, the humble-minded and the lowly through the obedience not only us, but also the before us generations better made, both those who received the oracles of him in fear and truth. Of many therefore and great and glorious having shared deeds, let us run back to the from [the] beginning handed down to us of peace goal, and let us gaze at the father and creator of the whole world and to the magnificent and surpassing of him gifts of peace and benefits let us cling. Let us see him according to thought and let us look with the eyes of the soul at the patient of him will; let us understand, how without anger he is toward all the creation of him.

choices.why: The two neuter substantivized adjectives name the virtues as abstract qualities, not persons; 'humility' matches the glossary for ταπεινοφροσύνη, and 'lowliness' keeps the second term distinct without importing 'meekness' or 'modesty'.
λόγια refers to divine utterances or sayings, not just 'words'; 'oracles' preserves the sacred, spoken character of what was received.
The compound verb conveys a return to a prior point; 'run back' keeps the urgency and the prefix ἐπ-ανα-.
σκοπός is the mark or target one aims at; 'goal' fits the athletic metaphor of running back to it.
κολλάομαι means to be joined or glued to something; 'cling' conveys the close, personal attachment to God's gifts and benefits.
The alpha-privative adjective negates ὀργή; 'free from anger' is more natural than 'without anger' while keeping the negation explicit.

pass_b_english: So many examples, and such great ones, have been attested in this way. Through obedience, humility and lowliness have made better not only us, but also the generations before us, those who received God's oracles in fear and truth.

Since we have shared in many great and glorious deeds, let us run back to the goal of peace that was handed down to us from the beginning. Let us gaze upon the Father and Creator of the whole world, and let us cling to his magnificent and surpassing gifts of peace and his acts of kindness.
Let us see him with our understanding, and let us look with the eyes of the soul at his patient will. Let us consider how free from anger he is toward all his creation.

problems.quote: Humility and lowliness through obedience have made better
problems.source_quote: Τῶν τοσούτων οὖν καὶ τοιούτων οὕτως μεμαρτυρημένων
problems.why: Missing opening clause 'With so many and such great examples having thus been attested/borne witness to'.
problems.fix: With so many and such great examples thus attested, humility and submissiveness through obedience have made better
problems.ruling: Τῶν τοσούτων οὖν καὶ τοιούτων οὕτως μεμαρτυρημένων is entirely omitted, losing the opening concessive clause about testified examples.

edits.old: Humility and lowliness through obedience have made better
edits.new: With so many and such great examples thus attested, humility and lowliness through obedience have made better

polish.changed: Clarified the opening sentence by separating the attested examples from the effect of humility and lowliness, and made the implied subject of 'received' explicit as 'God's oracles'.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'ταπεινοφροσύνη' as 'humility'; 'lowliness' is banned for ταπεινοφροσύνη.
last_rejected.ruling: τὸ ταπεινόφρον rendered 'humility' is within normal range; glossary concerns ταπεινοφροσύνη, not this adjective.

last_rejected.why: 'lowliness' is banned for ταπεινοφροσύνη; ὑποδεὲς means submissive/lowly, not the glossary term.
last_rejected.ruling: ὑποδεὲς means lowly/lowly-minded; 'lowliness' fits normal range; ban applies to ταπεινοφροσύνη, not ὑποδεὲς.
